title: Actions against Educators for Sexual Misconduct
what_it_is: Actions against Educators for Sexual Misconduct

sections.label: Educator sexual misconduct cases handling
sections.summary: Over five years, 14 educator sexual misconduct cases were reported to Police and prosecuted; officers are suspended during investigations and dismissed or redeployed if cases are inconclusive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (a) how many cases of educator sexual misconduct have been reported and investigated over the past five years; (b) how many of these cases have been inconclusive after investigations and what action has been taken; (c) what steps have been taken to monitor the conduct of teachers whose cases have been found inconclusive; and (d) what steps have been taken to separate the teachers from the students in these inconclusive cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education) (Schools)
sentences.text: We take every case reported to us very seriously and all such allegations are reported to the Police.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education) (Schools)
sentences.text: Officers are suspended from service while investigations take place, so that they are separated from students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education) (Schools)
sentences.text: Those found guilty are not allowed to remain in service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education) (Schools)
sentences.text: Page: 19 For cases where it is inconclusive whether there has been any sexual misconduct but it is established that there has been a serious breach of professional boundaries, officers will still be dismissed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education) (Schools)
sentences.text: In the very minority of cases where there is insufficient evidence to mount a case for either sexual or professional misconduct, but there remains sufficient evidence to raise genuine concerns, officers will be redeployed to jobs that do not require them to interact with students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education) (Schools)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, there have been 14 such cases of sexual misconduct that have been reported to the Police and prosecuted in Court.

sections.label: Student and teacher misconduct reporting
sections.summary: Students learn about appropriate adult behaviour and grooming from Primary 1, and teachers must report misconduct by other teachers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: From the point of view of students, appropriate behaviour from adults dealing with issues of sexual misconduct, predatory relationships, grooming – these discussions are started in Primary 1 and carried on throughout the whole of the schooling years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Students are told to look out for each other.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And then, if I can come back, the professionals, teachers and educators are also told that, if they are aware of misconduct by another teacher, it is their duty and their responsibility to make sure that it is reported.
